title: BUILD_PLAN
description: Structured build plan produced by the planning phase before any code is generated

planning_notes.description: LLM design reasoning: part decomposition choices, material decisions, dimension sources

intent.description: Plain-English description of what is being built and why

optimize_for.description: Plan-level print-orientation objective. 'strength' (default when omitted) keeps the part's load in the layer plane; 'min_support' minimizes support material; 'visual_quality' favors clean visible surfaces (penalizes gentle inclines under 45 deg, orients the cosmetic show_face against the bed). A per-part optimize_for overrides this for that part.

request_log.description: Append-only verbatim log of the user's request history: the initial request, plus every clarification or correction given during planning or the build. Optional; existing plans without it remain valid. When present, entries are never rewritten, reordered, or removed -- only appended.

parts.description: Ordered list of parts to generate

id.description: Unique snake_case identifier, used as script filename

interfaces.description: Physical connection points with external objects

type.description: Interface category (port_cutout, screw_mount, pcb_mount, snap_fit, etc.)

connector.description: Connector or standard name for this interface, e.g. usb_c

wall.description: Face the interface sits on (descriptive, e.g. north/south/top)

clearance_mm.description: Per-mate fit clearance for this interface, in mm

position_mm.description: Feature center in the part's authored frame [x, y, z] in mm; enables the deterministic feature-presence check

diameter_mm.description: Round-feature diameter in mm (feature-presence size target)

size_mm.description: Rectangular-feature [w, h] in mm (feature-presence size target)

blocks_needed.description: Blocks from inventory.json required for this part. Each item is either a block name string, or an object carrying the block name plus its instance extents (enables the script-level thin-block DFM check before any code is generated).

extents_mm.description: Block instance bounding box [x, y, z] in mm

part_notes.description: LLM reasoning for this part: blocks chosen, geometry written from scratch, unusual decisions

plate.description: Print-group id. Parts sharing a plate print in one job (print-in-place). Defaults to the part's own id (one part per plate) when omitted.

unions.description: Optional named unions this part's script produces. When present, the script's top-level `result` MUST be a dict mapping each union id to its CadQuery Workplane. When absent, the part is a single union whose id is the part id and whose plate is the part's `plate` (the default). The part's `placement` applies to every union it produces; union ids are unique across the model and are the namespace that `kinematics.moving_union` and plate grouping reference.

id.description: Unique snake_case union id; the per-union STL/object name and the kinematics/plate reference key

plate.description: Print-group id for this union; defaults to the part's `plate`, else the union id

load.description: Principal load direction (and type) in the part's own authored frame, determined by the planner (rule 10). Drives print-orientation strength scoring: for tension/bending/shear, orientations that keep this direction in the layer plane (perpendicular to build Z) score stronger; for compression, strength is orientation-neutral since a resting load doesn't stress the interlayer bond. Omitting the whole `load` object makes strength orientation-neutral (the optimizer does NOT guess a load axis from geometry) -- only correct when the part truly carries no structural load.

dir.description: Direction vector [x, y, z] in the authored frame; need not be unit length

type.description: Load type. tension/bending/shear keep layer-plane strength scoring (default, conservative). compression (a resting weight pressing straight through the part's thickness -- a base, plinth, pedestal, foot) makes strength orientation-neutral so support/bed-contact decide instead.

optimize_for.description: Per-part print-orientation objective; overrides the plan-level optimize_for for this part. Omit to inherit the plan-level value (or 'strength' when that is also absent).

show_face.description: Optional outward normal of the part's primary cosmetic surface in its own authored frame. Used by the 'visual_quality' optimization mode as the surface to orient face-down against the smooth bed. Omit to let the optimizer infer a cosmetic surface from geometry.

dir.description: Direction vector [x, y, z] in the authored frame; need not be unit length

placement.description: Pose of this union in the shared assembled frame. Rotations apply in listed order, then the translation. Omit for identity (union authored directly in the assembled frame). A part reached via a `joints` mate chain (see `joints`) MUST NOT declare its own placement -- its pose is derived.

kinematics.description: Declared range-of-motion checks for articulating joints, nested into a tree via `children`. Each entry sweeps its moving union (plus everything nested under its `children`) through its required range against every union outside that subtree. Optional; absent or empty skips the kinematic stage.

request_log.description: Append-only verbatim request history: the initial request plus every clarification/correction that shaped the plan. Optional; absent plans (including eval-corpus goldens) stay valid. When present, exactly one `initial` entry, first in the array (enforced by plan_validate.py, not expressible cleanly in draft-7).

root_part.description: The one part anchored directly into the world: its own `placement` (identity when absent) is its edge into the assembled frame. Required when `joints` is non-empty; every other part named in a `joints` entry gets its pose derived along the mate chain from this part instead of declaring its own `placement`.

joints.description: Cross-part matched-pair joints. Each entry names a matched-pair block (one whose inventory descriptor carries `emits`) and its two members, each fusing into a named part. A mated part's assembled pose is derived by composing the mate chain from `root_part`, instead of that part declaring its own `placement`. Optional; absent or empty needs no `root_part` and leaves every part's placement mechanism unchanged.

block.description: Matched-pair block name from inventory.json (must carry `emits`)

params.description: Kwargs passed to the block's function call -- the single declared source for this pair's parameters

members.description: The block's two members, each fusing into a part. The two entries must reference the block's two distinct `emits` ids and two distinct parts.

member.description: One of the block's declared `emits` ids

part.description: Id of the part whose script fuses this member in

dock.description: This member's pose WITHIN its host part's own authored frame (not the assembled frame). Omit for identity.

wall_min_mm.description: Minimum wall thickness for DFM check

overhang_max_deg.description: Maximum overhang angle before support required

block.description: Joint block name from inventory.json (must carry a dof)

axis_origin_mm.description: Assembled-frame pivot point [x, y, z] in mm

required_range.description: Range [lo, hi] the design requires, RELATIVE to the union's authored pose (zero), in the field unit. May be negative and may straddle zero (e.g. [-30, 90]).

lo_inclusive.description: Whether the lower bound must be cleared (closed). False = open: lo need not be reached and a collision exactly at lo is not reported.

hi_inclusive.description: Whether the upper bound must be cleared (closed). False = open.

step.description: Sweep increment in the derived unit (deg for revolute/spherical, mm for prismatic)

children.description: Nested kinematics entries mounted on this entry's moving_union, recursively forming the joint tree. Omitted/empty means nothing else is mounted on this joint. An entry not listed in any other entry's children is itself mounted on the static frame.

translate_mm.description: Translation [x, y, z] in mm, applied after rotations

rotate.description: Ordered rotation steps about axes through the origin
